rationale: Extend the compaction lead to the other producer the trim child's discriminator names, with sources rather than another execution. The snapshot path takes a user-supplied index and compares it against the leader's decided index (with the StopSign-adjusted decided log as the value used when the request equals the decided index), not against any recorded accepted index; with the witnessed drift the decided index is itself inflated, so this bound is reachable too, and the snapshot is then built from the entries the storage returns for a range that starts at the current compacted index, which an inflated bound can place past the entries a replica still holds. A child question is registered for that producer with its sources and a source-only unresolved interpretation, and its discriminator names the decisive observations (a snapshot accepted past the content, and what a reader then sees for the compacted region).

investigations.question: Does the snapshot path let a drifted decided index compact past the entries a replica still holds? The documented note says only up to the decided index can be snapshotted, and the implementation compares the user's index against the leader's decided index and then builds a snapshot from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index; both of those values can be inflated by the same drift, so a snapshot request can be accepted for an index above the entries in the log.
investigations.hypothesis: After the drift, snapshot(Some(index)) is accepted for an index up to the drifted decided index, and the snapshot is created from a storage range whose start is at or near the empty part of the log, so the resulting snapshot contains none of the entries a replica holds while the compacted index is advanced past them; readers of the decided region then see the snapshot instead of the entries, and the entries are no longer reachable through the log.
investigations.discriminator: Sampling a leader's snapshot call after the drift: the call's result, the reported compacted index, and what a read of the region below it returns for each node (an empty or snapshot entry rather than the decided entries), with the same read taken before the call.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only lead, opened because it is a different producer from the trim path that already produced a witnessed over-compaction. try_snapshot compares a user-supplied index against the leader's decided index (internal_storage.rs 432-453), and the documented note in the same function's caller states what may be snapshotted (mod.rs 180-184); the witnessed drift lifts that decided index above the content, so the comparison no longer keeps the request inside the entries a replica holds. create_snapshot then builds the snapshot from the storage range starting at the current compacted index (internal_storage.rs 367-383), and the in-memory storage returns an empty vector when the range does not exist (memory_storage.rs 92-107), so a request whose range lies past the entries would store a snapshot created from nothing while advancing the compacted index. What keeps this unresolved rather than asserted: the drift in the observed runs was produced with the same sealed configuration and a StopSign, where try_snapshot's equal case maps the decided index to the decided log without the StopSign, which lowered the effective bound in the states I sampled; and no snapshot call has been executed after a drift, so neither the acceptance of such a request nor what a reader then sees has been observed.
counterevidence: No snapshot call has been executed after a drift, so the acceptance of a request above the content and the content of the produced snapshot are inferred from the range arithmetic rather than observed.

In the observed drifted states the StopSign adjustment of the equal case lowers the effective bound, which may keep ordinary requests inside the entries; only requests strictly inside the drifted decided index would not be affected by that adjustment.
limitations: No execution for this account: only the derivation, the documented note and the storage arithmetic are cited.

The consequence I describe (readers seeing a snapshot instead of the entries) depends on the entry type's Snapshot implementation; the entry types used in this investigation keep their snapshots empty for empty ranges, which was not exercised here.
The snapshot path also forwards the request to peers, whose own decided indexes may differ; that interaction was not analysed here.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot path bounds a user-supplied index by the leader's decided index, not by any recorded accepted index and not by another node's decided index: an index equal to the decided index is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, an index below it is used as given, and a greater index is refused with the decided index reported. The snapshot itself is then created from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader or follower role; reached from the public snapshot() with Some(index) or None. Sourced from the captured snapshot; in the same investigation the decided index is witnessed to drift above the content, so this bound shares the drift's input. No snapshot has been called after a drift.
